summary_hint: <borrower> LOE dated <letter_date> to <recipient_or_lender> explaining <application_issue_type> re: <application_section_or_question>: <one-line reason>; status <current_status>, signed <yes/no>.

typed_core.name: borrower_name
typed_core.why: identity: whose explanation this is; attaches the LOE to a borrower

typed_core.name: borrower_name_2
typed_core.why: identity: co-borrower when the letter is jointly authored

typed_core.name: letter_date
typed_core.why: identity/processor: the date the explanation was written; recency of the resolution
typed_core.prompt_hint: Report the letter date separately from the signature date and from any dates inside the explanation

typed_core.name: recipient_or_lender_name
typed_core.why: identity: to whom the letter is addressed — confirms it is directed at this lender/file

typed_core.name: issuer_name
typed_core.why: processor: originating party when a third party (attorney/CPA) drafts the LOE — independence signal

typed_core.name: application_issue_type
typed_core.why: disambiguator: what kind of application item this addresses (undisclosed debt, address gap, name variation, large deposit) — the category a processor routes on

typed_core.name: application_section_or_question
typed_core.why: disambiguator: which 1003/URLA section or question the letter answers — ties the LOE to the exact application line it clears

typed_core.name: facts_being_explained
typed_core.why: processor: the specific application facts/discrepancy the letter addresses

typed_core.name: reason_or_root_cause
typed_core.why: processor: the borrower's stated cause — the substance an underwriter weighs
typed_core.prompt_hint: Do not force the borrower's prose into rigid fields — capture the cause faithfully in reason_or_root_cause / facts_being_explained

typed_core.name: corrective_action_or_resolution
typed_core.why: processor: what the borrower did/will do — whether the item is resolved

typed_core.name: current_status
typed_core.why: processor: resolved / ongoing / one-time — the completeness signal

typed_core.name: future_expectation_or_recurrence
typed_core.why: processor: whether the situation is expected to recur (a pattern vs isolated) — underwriter cares

typed_core.name: accuracy_certification
typed_core.why: processor: the attestation clause is present — a completeness check an underwriter performs
typed_core.prompt_hint: Capture the certification clause and signature presence as separate yes/no signals; do NOT judge whether the explanation is sufficient

typed_core.name: borrower_signature_present
typed_core.why: processor: scalar signature-present indicator; whether the LOE is executed

typed_core.name: borrower_signature_date
typed_core.why: processor: the execution date; distinct from letter_date

typed_core.name: preparer_name
typed_core.why: processor: who prepared the letter when not the borrower (attorney/LO) — independence

typed_core.name: property_address
typed_core.why: identity: subject property, when stated, links the LOE to the loan file

typed_core.name: loan_number
typed_core.why: identity: links the LOE to the loan file (confidential)

nested_lists.name: event_chronology
nested_lists.shape_reason: a chronology of dated events genuinely repeats and is the natural repeating structure of an explanation (e.g. a sequence of address moves, or the timeline of a resolved dispute); flat rows are light and sufficient

fields.name: event
fields.why: the event in the explanation's timeline

rejected.name: document_title, form_number, form_revision_date, document_status_or_version
rejected.reason: an LOE is free-form prose, not a standardized form

rejected.name: document_issue_date, effective_date, expiration_date, statement_period_start, statement_period_end
rejected.reason: duplicate letter_date; an LOE has no coverage period

rejected.name: party_names, party_addresses
rejected.reason: redundant — the party is the borrower (borrower_names)

rejected.name: account_case_reference_number
rejected.reason: not present on an application LOE; the loan is keyed by loan_number

rejected.name: signature_blocks, notary_block
rejected.reason: an application LOE is not notarized; execution captured via the two borrower_signature_* fields

rejected.name: supporting_document_list
rejected.reason: kept as a flat catch-all/simple list, not promoted to typed core — no rule reads the named docs (see Open questions)

rejected.name: relevant_amounts_accounts_or_addresses
rejected.reason: an object[] with no consumer; deferred (see Open questions)

rejected.name: preparer contact (phone/email portion of preparer_name_and_contact)
rejected.reason: contact detail with no consumer; only preparer_name retained

encoding_variations: Issue type: 'letter of explanation for undisclosed debt', 'address discrepancy', 'name variation', 'gap in employment on application' — application_issue_type degrades to text and must travel beside application_section_or_question so the router knows which application line it clears
Three distinct dates: letter_date (when written), the dated rows in event_chronology (when things happened), and borrower_signature_date (when executed) — borrowers blur these; keep them separate

Certification vs signature: the attestation clause (accuracy_certification) and the physical signature (borrower_signature_present) are two separate completeness elements — an LOE can have one without the other

open_questions.q: No rule consumes this document today (Tier 3, rule_count 0). The field set is sized for a likely future application-completeness/discrepancy rule
options: trim if the LOE is merged into a single generic LOE module
open_questions.recommendation: keep the ~18-field set so a future rule can be built without re-extraction (the IH-1 lesson); trim only if the LOE is merged into a single generic LOE module

open_questions.q: Nested-list choice. Three catalog fields repeat: event_chronology (object[]), supporting_document_list (string[]), relevant_amounts_accounts_or_addresses (object[]). Budget is one nested list
open_questions.recommendation: event_chronology as the nested list, supporting_document_list as a light flat str[], and defer relevant_amounts_accounts_or_addresses to the catch-all until a rule needs it (then it needs its own redactor for PII)
degrade to str and add a prompt hint; add a bool coercer only if a rule branches on them

open_questions.q: Generic vs specialized LOE module. This overlaps the credit LOE (#019) and other LOE variants
options: a shared LOE core with variant-specific fields
open_questions.recommendation: a shared LOE core (borrower, dates, signature, cause) with variant-specific fields (application_section_or_question here) rather than a fully separate module

notes: Serves 0 rules (no rule references this document type today); this is a free-form explanatory letter. Every field is justified by identity (#3), processor review (#4), or a disambiguator (#5). No PII beyond names.
This is the application-discrepancy LOE variant (distinct from the credit LOE #019). Center extraction on the application item being explained: which section/question, what fact, why.
No PII beyond borrower_name / borrower_name_2 (standard-sensitivity names), acceptable as typed core, not registered.

relevant_amounts_accounts_or_addresses (deferred to catch-all) could contain an account number or address — if promoted, an account element there would need masking/registration and must NOT be left to the unmasked catch-all.
Do NOT judge whether the explanation is sufficient — that is an underwriter/rule call (tags describe, rules judge).
